t: The Mexica founded Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco in 1325 or 1327, and in 1521 Spanish forces and their Indigenous allies besieged and razed it, and Cuauhtémoc surrendered in August.

Cortés founded the Spanish capital on the ruins, and for three centuries Mexico City was the seat of the viceroyalty of New Spain, its archbishopric and its merchants, and afterwards the capital of independent Mexico.

The city sat on a lake bed with no natural outlet, so floods led to a drainage works begun in 1607 and finished under Porfirio Díaz, while later growth overflowed the Federal District and the soft clay began to sink.
dyk: The colonial city was built on the saturated clay of the former lake bed, and since the beginning of the 20th century it has sunk as much as nine metres in some areas and continues to sink almost 50 centimetres a year.
ev: The Mexica found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco, a date some sources give as 1327
Cuauhtémoc surrenders after the three-month siege and Tenochtitlan is razed, and Cortés refounds the city as Mexico
Thousands of Indigenous workers are drafted to dig the first Desagüe, the drainage ditch and tunnel
The Army of the Three Guarantees enters the city and Mexico is declared independent
United States troops under Winfield Scott take the city after the battles of Molino del Rey and Chapultepec
The Decena Trágica ends with the coup of Victoriano Huerta and the killing of Francisco Madero
An earthquake of magnitude 8.1 collapses hundreds of buildings
The city elects its mayor for the first time since 1928

f.founded: Founded as Tenochtitlan by the Mexica in 1325 or 1327, on an island in Lake Texcoco; the Spanish razed it in 1521 and Hernán Cortés founded the Spanish colonial capital on the site.
f.where: In the Valley of Mexico, a basin on the high plateaus of south-central Mexico, at an altitude of about 2,240 metres, on the bed of the former Lake Texcoco.
f.known: The Mexica city of Tenochtitlan and its siege and destruction in 1521; the capital of New Spain; the Zócalo and the Metropolitan Cathedral; the Desagüe, the long effort to drain the valley; the capital of independent Mexico; the muralists; the earthquake of 1985
f.today: Mexico City, officially Ciudad de México or CDMX since 2016, is the capital and largest city of Mexico and is divided into 16 boroughs.
